newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Nelson Gold to up gold output at Tajik mine.
newsitem.headline: Nelson Gold to up gold output at Tajik mine.

text.p: Toronto-listed Nelson Gold Corporation Ltd said on Friday it planned to boost gold output at a mine in Tajikistan to 72,000 ounces this year and up to 100,000 ounces by 1998.
Nelson said its Tajik production, which began in the first quarter of 1996, totalled 44,448 ounces.

"Nelson Gold Corporation is pleased to announce the decision to proceed with...the expansion of the existing mining, milling and carbon-in-leach operations at the Zeravshan Gold Company," the company said in a statement sent to Reuters.
Expanding gold output would cost $11.03 million, the company said. Nelson previously had said it invested a total of $54 million in Tajikistan by the end of 1996.
Nelson holds a 49 percent stake in Zeravshan Gold, a joint venture with the former Soviet republic. It also manages and operates the project.
Tajikistan's government holds the remaining stake in the venture which exploits the Jilau deposit located in the north of the Central Asian state, near its border with Uzbekistan.
Tajikistan is a mountainous country of 5.7 million people and has been ravaged by four years of civil war.
